A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same model-merging research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G are available and support reliable comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of merged vision-language reward models, including benchmark accuracies in Table 1, image-input ablations, hyperparameter analyses, and qualitative results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results and additionally reports computation times for merging and validation in Section 4.4.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 and Appendix A correct the stated Task Arithmetic and TIES/DARE merge rules by adding the pretrained transformer parameters to the weighted task-vector updates. This changes the specified parameter reconstruction; the architecture and merging strategies remain the same, and an implementation change or experimental rerun is not documented.

E1.justification: Both versions use VL-RewardBench, TextVQA, MMMU-Pro Standard and Vision, and RLAIF-V for validation. The represented domains, multimodal judging tasks, and Best-of-N evaluation scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the same LVLM, text-based reward model, Random, and Cascade baselines. v2 Table 2 redisplays selected comparisons already present in v1 Appendix Table 11, whose full contents remain in v2 Table 12.

E3.justification: The model configurations, hyperparameter grids, 400-instance validation set with 100 additional tie-breaking instances, and Best-of-8 generation settings are retained. Appendices A–D preserve the sampling settings and prompts. The new hardware and timing descriptions do not establish changes to these evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 adds a computational-overhead analysis comparing the time required by merging strategies and validation. The image-removal ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity analyses, and four qualitative cases in Appendices F–G are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the authors' results. Seed and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged; the additional validation samples used to resolve ties were already documented in v1.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports approximately 1.5 CPU hours for weighted averaging and task arithmetic sweeps, 6 for TIES, 3 for DARE, and 1.5 GPU hours per method for validation. Benchmark accuracies, qualitative reward scores, and plotted findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices.

T1.justification: The equations in Section 3.2 and Appendix A restore the omitted pretrained-weight term in Task Arithmetic and TIES/DARE. This corrects the mathematical definitions; for example, Task Arithmetic at lambda = 0 now recovers pretrained transformer weights rather than zero weights. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of training-free textual-preference transfer and improved multimodal reward assessment. The claim of competitiveness with larger and commercial models already appeared in v1 Section 4.3 and Appendix G.1.

C2.justification: The new overhead discussion argues that CPU-based merging and modest validation requirements keep computational cost low, and that parallel execution can reduce elapsed time. Existing interpretations of visual input and hyperparameter effects, together with the stated applicability and computational limitations, are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project code/data repository link in the abstract and identifies the computation hardware: Intel Xeon Silver 4216 CPUs with 128 GB RAM and RTX 3090 GPUs with 24 GB memory. It also supplies merging and validation runtimes, extending the implementation information available in v1.

R1.justification: The research reference list and positioning relative to preference learning, LVLM judging, and model merging are unchanged. The added figure-icon source credit does not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds the computational-overhead subsection, acknowledgements, and brief abstract and caption material, with limited wording edits. Most prose and the section sequence remain unchanged; there is no extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds a condensed main-text comparison table using existing appendix results, relocates Figure 2, and adds an icon-source credit to Figure 1. Subsequent tables are renumbered and pages reflow. Existing plots and qualitative examples retain their content.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the omitted pretrained-weight terms and improves reproducibility information through hardware, runtime, and code/data access details. Its main-text comparison table also makes existing evidence easier to inspect. These are useful, bounded gains: benchmark evidence remains unchanged, and the new claim of lower cost than training from scratch lacks a measured training baseline.
